text:
Sam: FYI repro'd a sharp p99 tail during the 11:30 load run. Pattern looks like KV churn + kernel-selection flips under heavy conc.
Maria: numbers? how bad?
Sam: baseline p99 ~210ms, peaked ~920ms at 8k conc for small-chat profile. p95 drifted ~20-40ms only.
Tayler: recall we landed two changes last week: (1) kernel-selection prefers fused-attn for seq<=128, (2) microbatch max increased 32->48. Could be combined effect.
Joe: also had canary flag evict-on-pressure=true. Under heavy concurrency eviction rate spiked and eviction path holds mempool lock (~1ms each).
perf-bot: quick sample @1794512100
```
- kv::evict_path 28%
- microbatch::assemble 20%
- kernels::fused_attn::prepare 16%
- scheduler::enqueue 14%
- request_handler 8%
```
Maria: fused_attn::prepare showing up is suspicious. Maybe fused path does extra setup allocations that weren't amortized when batches became heterogeneous.
Tayler: I ran a local repro with flamegraphs: when kv_hit < 75% microbatch queueing time increases and average seq-length variance goes up -> selection flips to fused more often. Fused setup cost is non-trivial.
Sam: concise causal chain hypothesis: high conc -> KV misses/evictions -> mempool contention + longer per-request work -> microbatcher groups diverse seqs -> kernel selection flips to higher-setup kernels -> p99 tail.
Joe: short mitigation options: revert microbatch max to 32, temporarily disable fused kernel on canary, reduce eviction aggressiveness. Which low-risk moves first?
Maria: let's do (A) revert microbatch max to 32 via config rollout (fast) and (B) add alerting: kv_eviction_rate and kernel_prepare_p90. Also add per-batch setup_time metric.
Tayler: add a transient kernel-selection override: force selection stable by seq-length for 30m on canary to avoid mixed batches.
Joe: I'll prepare canary plan: revert mb_max on dedicated pools + set kernel_override flag. Canary 30m.
perf-bot: canary-run summary @1794513000
```
run: canary-1794513000
- concurrency: 8000
- kv_hit_rate: 72% -> 91% after revert
- p95: 245ms -> 238ms
- p99: 920ms -> 300ms
- evictions/s: 65 -> 10
```
Sam: big p99 improvement. Revert looks effective as mitigation but still need root cause investigation.
Tayler: root tasks: instrument kernel-selection to emit decision reason (seq_cutoff, kv_delta, quant_path), tag batch with seq-entropy, and expose per-batch setup_time. Will add logging sampling to avoid noise.
Maria: filing follow-ups: KERNEL-125 (selection telemetry), MB-460 (batch-sizing experiments), KV-801 (eviction tuning). Linking notes: https://go/infra/KERNEL-125
Joe: experimental matrix proposal: mb_max in [24,32,40,48], eviction_threshold in [60,70,80], fused_kernel [on,off]. Measure p95/p99 and net throughput.
Sam: also check mempool lock hold-time distribution. If evictions serialize, consider async batch-evict or coalesced eviction.
Tayler: observation: merged batches with high kernel-entropy amplify setup_time. We should consider a microbatch heuristic: if predicted setup_cost > X ms and batch has high entropy, prefer smaller homogeneous batches.
Maria: propose quick heuristic: if kernel_entropy > 0.35 -> cap batch_size *= 0.7. Might trade throughput for p99.
Joe: prototyping: batch_predictor -> estimate entropy -> apply cap. Scheduling experiment scheduled.
perf-bot: scheduled experiment 1794513400
```
config: entropy_cap=true, cap_ratio=0.7
expectation: p99 down ~40% at cost ~5-10% throughput
```
Sam: roll entropic cap to canary and monitor. Thx all. :thumbsup:
Maria: ack, will wire dashboards + temp paging for kv_eviction_rate.
Tayler: will attach flamegraphs + short writeup after canary completes.
Joe: rolling revert + kernel override now (starting 1794513350).
perf-bot: deploy complete 1794513395
Sam: keeping thread open for final metrics + writeup. Close when writeup attached.
